title: What is a Cloud Data Warehouse?

scenes.heading: What is a Cloud Data Warehouse?
scenes.narration: A cloud data warehouse is a fully managed analytics database that stores and queries huge volumes of structured data on demand.

scenes.heading: What makes it different
bullets: Analytics-first: optimized for scanning and aggregating billions of rows, not single-row transactions.
Fully managed: the cloud provider handles hardware, patching, backups, and scaling for you.
Elastic: storage and compute grow independently, so you pay for what you actually use.
SQL-native: analysts query it with familiar SQL instead of writing custom code.
scenes.narration: It is built for analytics rather than transactions, so it excels at scanning and aggregating billions of rows. Because it is fully managed and elastic, you skip hardware operations and scale compute on demand. And since it speaks SQL, existing analysts can be productive immediately.

scenes.heading: From raw data to insight
scenes.narration: Data flows in from applications, files, and event streams, then lands in the warehouse. From there teams model it with SQL and expose it to dashboards and machine learning. The warehouse is the central hub that turns scattered data into trusted insight.

scenes.heading: Warehouse vs operational database
scenes.narration: An operational database is tuned for many tiny transactions that keep an app running. A warehouse instead scans wide slices of history to answer analytical questions. Reach for the warehouse when you need trends across millions of rows, not the latest order status.

scenes.text: A cloud data warehouse is your managed, elastic, SQL-driven home for analytics at scale.
scenes.narration: Remember that the warehouse is the managed, elastic, SQL-driven foundation your entire analytics stack builds on.
